name: Modal
description: A dialog over the page that blocks interaction until dismissed. Works on <dialog> (preferred, opened with showModal()) or on a <div role="dialog">.

elements.name: backdrop
elements.description: Dimmed layer behind the dialog; clicking it may close the modal.

elements.name: header
elements.description: Holds the title and close button.

elements.name: close
elements.description: Icon button that closes the dialog.

elements.name: footer
elements.description: Actions, right-aligned. Put the primary action last.

states.name: closed
states.description: Hidden (div form). With <dialog>, use the open attribute / showModal() instead.
states.pair: When closed, return focus to the control that opened the modal.

children: c-modal contains c-modal__backdrop and c-modal__container as siblings.
c-modal__container contains header, body and footer in that order.

use: Use for short, focused tasks: confirmations, small forms.
Buttons in c-modal__footer are c-button; the footer provides the gap. Use c-button--danger for destructive confirmations.
avoid: Opening a modal from another modal.
Long, scrolling content; use a page instead.

a11y: Prefer <dialog class="c-modal"> opened with showModal(): the browser then handles focus, Escape and inertness. With a <div>, set role="dialog", aria-modal="true" and manage focus yourself.
With the <div> form, make the page behind inert and lock scrolling while open, trap focus, close on Escape, and return focus to the opener.
c-modal__close needs aria-label="Close" and an SVG icon, not a text glyph.
